title: Figma vs Sketch: Compare Design Workflows Before Switching
description: A workflow-based Figma vs Sketch comparison covering collaboration, prototyping, design systems, platform needs, handoff, administration and migration. PilotStack has not independently verified current prices or ratings; confirm current capabilities and plans with each vendor.

features.name: Collaboration and review
features.tool1: Run the same multi-person design review and record comment, handoff and version-control friction.
features.tool2: Run the same multi-person design review and record comment, handoff and version-control friction.
features.tool1Detail: Test how designers, product managers and developers review changes, resolve feedback, and identify the approved version. Confirm guest access, permissions and plan limits.
features.tool2Detail: Use the same review scenario and confirm the current collaboration model, permissions, version history and any plan-specific restrictions.

features.name: Design systems and components
features.tool1: Rebuild a representative component set and update shared styles or variants.
features.tool2: Rebuild the same component set and update shared styles or variants.
features.tool1Detail: Measure how reliably the team can reuse components, document design tokens and roll out changes without breaking existing work.
features.tool2Detail: Measure the same tasks, including component reuse, shared styles, library updates and how the team manages consistency.

features.name: Prototyping and handoff
features.tool1: Prototype one key user journey and hand it to a developer.
features.tool2: Prototype the same user journey and hand it to a developer.
features.tool1Detail: Check interaction needs, inspectable specs, asset export, developer access and the amount of manual explanation required.
features.tool2Detail: Check the same interaction needs, specs, asset export, developer access and manual handoff effort.

features.name: Platform and working conditions
features.tool1: Verify supported devices, browser/desktop requirements and offline expectations for your team.
features.tool2: Verify supported devices, macOS requirements and offline expectations for your team.
features.tool1Detail: Test the actual devices and network conditions used by the team. Confirm supported versions and whether critical tasks work without connectivity.
features.tool2Detail: Test the actual devices and network conditions used by the team. Confirm supported versions and whether critical tasks work without connectivity.

features.name: Administration and governance
features.tool1: Review access controls, workspace ownership, retention and export options.
features.tool2: Review access controls, workspace ownership, retention and export options.
features.tool1Detail: Ask who can invite users, change permissions, manage libraries, export files and remove access when a person leaves.
features.tool2Detail: Ask who can invite users, change permissions, manage libraries, export files and remove access when a person leaves.

features.name: Cost and migration
features.tool1: Request a quote for the expected seats, roles, collaboration and admin needs.
features.tool2: Request a quote for the same seats, roles, collaboration and admin needs.
features.tool1Detail: Include paid seats, guests, required add-ons, implementation, training and the cost of migrating existing design files.
features.tool2Detail: Use equivalent assumptions and include paid seats, add-ons, migration, training and the cost of maintaining old files.

verdict: There is no universal winner for every design team. Compare the products using the same design task, component library, prototype, handoff and review process. A team that prioritizes cross-functional collaboration may weigh different factors from a team whose work is centered on a native macOS workflow. Verify current platform support, collaboration limits, offline behavior, export options, permissions and pricing with the vendors before deciding. This is a buyer guide, not a controlled benchmark or hands-on test.

faqs.question: Is Figma better than Sketch?
faqs.answer: It depends on the team's collaboration model, platform requirements, design-system workflow, handoff needs and budget. Run the same representative tasks in both products and compare the friction and plan limitations before choosing.

faqs.question: Can a design team switch without losing work?
faqs.answer: Do a small migration pilot first. Check which files, components, libraries, comments, prototypes and version history transfer, and decide how the team will preserve or archive work that cannot be migrated cleanly.

faqs.question: How should we compare their prices?
faqs.answer: Request current pricing for the same number and type of seats, guests, admin requirements and any necessary add-ons. Confirm billing frequency and terms directly with each vendor; this page does not publish unverified price figures.
